title: Canada Lotto 6/49 Overview and Matrix
description:
Lotto 6/49 is Canada's long-running national lottery game. A play costs 3 Canadian dollars and includes one Classic selection of six numbers from 1 to 49, plus a 10-digit Gold Ball Draw number printed on the ticket. A draw produces six main numbers plus a bonus number drawn from the balls that remain, and matching all six main numbers wins the Classic jackpot.

The current matrix is 6 from 49 with a bonus number. The Classic jackpot is fixed at 5 million Canadian dollars for every draw: it does not roll over and does not grow. The growing jackpot in the game lives in the separate Gold Ball Draw, described in the matrix history and rollover records. Draws take place on Wednesday and Saturday evenings at about 10:30 pm Eastern Time. The exact jackpot odds for one Classic selection are 1 in 13,983,816.

Lottery outcomes are random. No method, pattern, chart, or number selection approach can predict a future draw, and every combination in a given draw has the same chance as every other combination in that draw. Frequency, hot, cold, and overdue counts describe past draws only; they do not change the chance of any number in the next draw.

demo.code:
from math import comb
def tier_odds(pool, pick, specs):
    # specs: list of (main matches, mode) where mode is "yes" (bonus must match),
    # "no" (bonus must not match), or "any" (bonus irrelevant for this tier).
    total = comb(pool, pick) * (pool - pick)
    rows = []
    for m, mode in specs:
        main = comb(pick, m) * comb(pool - pick, pick - m)
        if mode == "yes":
            bways = pick - m
        elif mode == "no":
            bways = (pool - pick) - (pick - m)
        else:
            bways = pool - pick
        ways = main * bways
        rows.append((m, mode, int(total / ways + 0.5)))
    return rows
def show(pool, pick, specs):
    for m, mode, odds in tier_odds(pool, pick, specs):
        label = str(m) + (" + bonus" if mode == "yes" else (" (bonus irrelevant)" if mode == "any" else ""))
        print(label + ": 1 in " + str(odds))

print("Lotto 6/49 jackpot combinations, 6 from 49:", comb(49, 6))
print("Classic jackpot odds per selection: 1 in " + str(comb(49, 6)))
print("Classic jackpot (Canadian dollars): 5000000")

title: Canada Lotto Max Prize Tiers and MaxMillions Mechanics
description:

title: Canada Lotto Matrix History
description:
Lotto 6/49 launched in June 1982 as Canada's first national game allowing players to select their own numbers. A Guaranteed Prize Draw side game, printing a 10-digit number on each ticket, was added in September 2013. On 14 September 2022 the game was split into two components on the same ticket: the Classic Draw, with a fixed 5 million dollar jackpot, and the Gold Ball Draw, which replaced the Guaranteed Prize Draw and carries the growing jackpot.

Lotto Max launched in September 2009 as a 7 from 49 game. In May 2019 it moved to 7 from 50, added a Tuesday draw alongside Friday, raised its cap from 60 million to 80 million dollars, and expanded its prize tiers. On 14 April 2026 it moved again to 7 from 52, four selections per 6 dollar play, a 90 million dollar cap, and the new MaxPlus layer. Tables and odds from any earlier format must be labeled with their format and date, never presented as current.

title: Canada Lotto Frequency Method and Simulated Set Demo
description:
The frequency method counts how often each number has appeared in past draws and ranks numbers from most frequent to least frequent. It is a descriptive summary of history: it answers the question of what has been drawn before, and it says nothing about what will be drawn next, because each draw is an independent random selection from the same pool.

The demo below runs on clearly labeled simulated draws, not on real Canadian draw history, because no verified real draw history was imported at build time. Two hundred simulated draws of six numbers from 1 to 49 are generated with a fixed seed, and the five most frequent simulated numbers are listed. The ranking changes with the seed and with the number of simulated draws, which is itself evidence that frequency in a sample is not a stable property of the numbers.

title: Canada Lotto Hot Numbers Method
description:
The hot numbers method selects numbers that have appeared most often in a chosen window of recent draws. The draw mechanism has no memory: the balls are not weighted by past appearances, and a number that appeared often in the last fifty draws has exactly the same chance as any other number in the next draw.

A hot list is therefore a report about a chosen window, and different windows give different hot lists. Changing the window, adding or removing a few draws, or starting the window one draw later can move a number on or off the list. The demo below illustrates that sensitivity on simulated data: it ranks simulated numbers over two different windows and shows that the rankings disagree. Any use of a hot list should be labeled as a description of the chosen window, never as a forecast.

Lottery outcomes are random. Frequency, hot, cold, and overdue counts describe past draws only; they do not change the chance of any number in the next draw.

title: Canada Lotto Cold and Overdue Numbers Method
description:
The cold and overdue method selects numbers that have appeared least often, or that have gone longest without appearing, on the theory that such numbers are due to appear. That theory is the gambler's fallacy applied to a lottery: a random draw does not compensate for past absences, and a number that has been absent for many draws is no more likely in the next draw than a number drawn in the previous draw.

Overdue counts are still useful as descriptive statistics. They show gaps in a chosen history, and long gaps are expected in random data: with 49 numbers and six drawn per draw, a typical number is absent from most draws, so gaps of many draws occur routinely without any mechanism behind them. The demo below counts, on simulated data, how many draws have passed since each of a few numbers last appeared, and labels the result as simulation only.

Lottery outcomes are random. No method, pattern, chart, or number selection approach can predict a future draw, and every combination in a given draw has the same chance as every other combination in that draw. Frequency, hot, cold, and overdue counts describe past draws only; they do not change the chance of any number in the next draw.

import random
random.seed(20261031)
draws = [sorted(random.sample(range(1, 50), 6)) for _ in range(100)]
for target in (7, 19, 33):
    gap = 0
    for d in reversed(draws):
        if target in d:
            break
        gap += 1
    print("Simulated gap for number " + str(target) + ": " + str(gap) + " draws since last simulated appearance")
print("Note: simulated data only, not real draw history. A gap does not raise the next-draw chance.")

title: Canada Lotto Rollover Patterns
description:
Rollover means different things in the two main Canadian games, and the difference is the point of this record. In Lotto 6/49, the Classic jackpot does not roll: it is fixed at 5 million dollars every draw, win or no win. The growing jackpot is the Gold Ball jackpot, which starts at 10 million dollars, grows by 2 million dollars after each draw in which the gold ball is not drawn, and is capped at 68 million dollars. The Gold Ball Draw uses 30 balls, one of which is gold, and one ball is removed after each draw in which the gold ball is not drawn, so the chance of drawing gold rises through a cycle.

In Lotto Max, the main jackpot does roll: it grows from 10 million dollars until it is won or reaches the 90 million dollar cap, and once it reaches 50 million dollars, extra 1 million dollar MaxMillions prizes are added. The demo below simulates a Gold Ball cycle with a fixed seed, drawing one ball per draw from a shrinking set until the gold ball appears, and labels the cycle as simulation only. A simulated cycle length says nothing about the length of any real cycle.

Lottery outcomes are random. No method, pattern, chart, or number selection approach can predict a future draw, and every combination in a given draw has the same chance as every other combination in that draw. Frequency, hot, cold, and overdue counts describe past draws only; they do not change the chance of any number in the next draw.

demo.code:
import random
random.seed(20261032)
balls = list(range(30))
jackpot = 10000000
draws = 0
while True:
    draws += 1
    pick = random.choice(balls)
    if pick == 0:
        break
    balls.remove(pick)
    jackpot += 2000000
    if jackpot > 68000000:
        jackpot = 68000000
print("Simulated Gold Ball cycle length (draws): " + str(draws))
print("Simulated Gold Ball jackpot at win (Canadian dollars): " + str(jackpot))
print("Note: simulated cycle only, not a real Gold Ball cycle.")

title: Canada Lotto Expected Value and Tax-Free Status, General Information Only
description:
Expected value is the average prize value of a play over a very large number of identical plays, computed as the sum over prize tiers of tier chance multiplied by tier prize, minus the price of the play. It is a teaching tool for comparing games and for showing why a lottery play, on average, returns less than its price. The demo below uses illustrative fixed prizes for the lower tiers and an illustrative jackpot, not current official prize amounts, because several Canadian tiers are variable and change with sales and winner counts.

On tax status, lottery prizes in Canada are generally treated as windfalls rather than income, so a lottery prize itself is generally not subject to Canadian income tax, and the full advertised prize is received by the winner. That general statement is not tax advice: income earned by investing winnings, such as interest, dividends, or capital gains, is taxable under ordinary rules, and individual circumstances should be confirmed with a qualified tax professional. This record gives general information only.

Frequency, hot, cold, and overdue counts describe past draws only; they do not change the chance of any number in the next draw.

title: Canada Lotto Verification Guide
description:
A ticket should be verified against the official result for its own draw, not against a summary or a result from another draw night. The official sources are the provincial and regional lottery corporations: the Ontario Lottery and Gaming Corporation, the British Columbia Lottery Corporation, the Western Canada Lottery Corporation, Loto-Quebec, the Atlantic Lottery Corporation, and the Interprovincial Lottery Corporation for the national games. Each corporation publishes results for the games it distributes, and the national result is the same across corporations for a given draw.

Four checks prevent the most common errors. First, confirm the game and the format date: Lotto Max results before 14 April 2026 belong to the 7 from 50 format, and results from that date belong to the 7 from 52 format; Lotto 6/49 results before 14 September 2022 belong to the single rolling jackpot, and later results split Classic and Gold Ball. Second, confirm the draw date and draw night. Third, check the main draw, the bonus tier, the Gold Ball or MaxMillions and MaxPlus layers, and any Encore or Extra add-on separately. Fourth, confirm the claim period, which is about one year from the draw date in each province, and keep the ticket until any prize claim is settled.

Lottery outcomes are random. No method, pattern, chart, or number selection approach can predict a future draw, and every combination in a given draw has the same chance as every other combination in that draw. Frequency, hot, cold, and overdue counts describe past draws only; they do not change the chance of any number in the next draw.

demo.code:
from math import comb
def tier_odds(pool, pick, specs):
    # specs: list of (main matches, mode) where mode is "yes" (bonus must match),
    # "no" (bonus must not match), or "any" (bonus irrelevant for this tier).
    total = comb(pool, pick) * (pool - pick)
    rows = []
    for m, mode in specs:
        main = comb(pick, m) * comb(pool - pick, pick - m)
        if mode == "yes":
            bways = pick - m
        elif mode == "no":
            bways = (pool - pick) - (pick - m)
        else:
            bways = pool - pick
        ways = main * bways
        rows.append((m, mode, int(total / ways + 0.5)))
    return rows
def show(pool, pick, specs):
    for m, mode, odds in tier_odds(pool, pick, specs):
        label = str(m) + (" + bonus" if mode == "yes" else (" (bonus irrelevant)" if mode == "any" else ""))
        print(label + ": 1 in " + str(odds))

print("Verification step 1: confirm game and format date")
print("Verification step 2: confirm draw date and draw night")
print("Verification step 3: check main draw, bonus tier, Gold Ball or Max layers, and add-on separately")
print("Verification step 4: confirm claim period, about one year from draw date")

title: Canada Lotto 6/49 Versus Lotto Max Comparison and Responsible Play
description:
Lotto 6/49 and Lotto Max differ in matrix, price, jackpot behavior, and odds. Lotto Max costs 6 dollars, uses four selections of seven numbers from 52, draws on Tuesday and Friday, offers a jackpot starting at 10 million dollars and capped at 90 million dollars plus MaxMillions and MaxPlus layers, and gives jackpot odds of 1 in 33,446,140 per play.

The shorter jackpot odds for 6/49 do not make any particular 6/49 line likely, and the larger Lotto Max jackpot does not make any particular Lotto Max selection likely.
